rights: Lightfoot–Harmer 1891 and Lake 1907 are the public-domain working texts. Bonner 1934 is consulted for scoped factual manuscript readings and lacunae; its full text, reconstructions, images and commentary are not vendored. The consultation copy carries a 1934 copyright notice.

sources.role: Printed transcription of one Athos codex; not independent votes for each edition.
Published transcription/apparatus of Michigan inv.917. Bracketed restoration and missing leaves are not counted as preserved manuscript words.

decisions.evidence_scope: Bonner printed p.113, papyrus page 53, line18: the suffering verb is outside restoration brackets. The surrounding gladly/be afflicted supplement is bracketed. Lake Plate X line9 confirms fear in A. Latin traditions report voluntary suffering; Coptic/Ethiopic support is reported but not directly checked here.
decisions.rationale: Prefer the attested suffering verb, with modest weight for the older Greek witness and versional semantic support. Do not insert willingness from an editor’s reconstruction into M. The composite working source retains the surrounding base wording; it is not a diplomatic transcript of M.

translation_candidates.selected: Some of them will also suffer, recognizing the deeds they have done. All of them will have their home in the tower.
translation_candidates.A_alternative: Some of them are also afraid, recognizing the deeds they have done. All of them will have their home in the tower.
translation_candidates.printed_conjecture_alternative: Some of them also suffer willingly, recognizing the deeds they have done. All of them will have their home in the tower.

decisions.uncertainty: The nonstandard Greek verb form has been interpreted as future or present. Reader note should preserve that uncertainty. Full direct image and versional collation remains pending.

decisions.evidence_scope: Lake Plate X line49 reads rock in A. Lightfoot apparatus reports E with rock, L1 with gate, L2 with both. Bonner p.120 leaves the decisive genitive in a lacuna: M is not a preserved rock/gate vote.
decisions.rationale: Retain the attested Greek rock reading, supported by a reported ancient version, rather than the working edition’s gate conjecture. The nearby description can mention both rock and gate without requiring identical wording here. The Latin gate and combined alternatives remain recorded; no reading is claimed from the damaged M genitive.

translation_candidates.selected: I saw six tall, glorious men arrive, alike in appearance. They called a crowd of men, who were tall, handsome, and strong. The six men ordered them to build a tower on top of the rock. The men who had come to build the tower made a great commotion as they ran here and there around the gate.
translation_candidates.L1_alternative: I saw six tall, glorious men arrive, alike in appearance. They called a crowd of men, who were tall, handsome, and strong. The six men ordered them to build a tower on top of the gate. The men who had come to build the tower made a great commotion as they ran here and there around the gate.

decisions.uncertainty: Direct ancient-version and Coptic comparison remains pending. The M reconstruction cannot establish the missing noun.

open_cases.observation: M has Greek material for the section omitted in A, with damaged letters and shorter categories. Some words of the longer nineteenth-century version-based reconstruction are absent from M.
open_cases.action: Do not call the whole section lost in Greek, and do not copy the longer reconstruction as M’s text. Compare the Latin traditions before selecting the category sequence.

open_cases.observation: The virtue construction in M is partly restored; manuscript and versional grammar alternatives remain distinct.
open_cases.action: Do not count a bracketed reconstruction as preserved Greek wording.

open_cases.observation: The Michigan edition marks a lost leaf after the beginning of the stones sentence, before the disputed negation/adjective.
open_cases.action: M cannot settle the inserted μὴ. Keep the insertion marked in the working source pending comparison with the specified parallel passages and versions.

limits: No complete critical collation of the book is claimed.
Edition-reported versional support is not direct reading of all the individual Latin/Ethiopic manuscripts.
The source selections do not by themselves publish new English or certify all other wording in either chapter.
